transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've been having these evenings where I just eat a huge amount of food. I'll buy a whole family-size takeout order on the way home, and then I usually add chips or bakery things from the store on top of that. And I end up eating most of it myself... usually before I even really seem to register how much is actually gone.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes, exactly. It's like... once I start eating, there's this awful switch that flips. I can literally be sitting there thinking to myself, *Taylor, put it away, you don't need this*, but my hands just keep opening containers. It's like I'm not even the one in charge anymore. I just can't stop.
Do these episodes of eating a huge amount of food usually happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset about something?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed a connection like that. I mean, sometimes I'm stressed, sure, but... it doesn't seem to only happen when I'm upset or anxious. A lot of times I've had a completely normal, fine day at the office, and I still end up doing it on the way home.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

Yes, I do. I feel terrible about it afterwards. I just look at all the empty containers and wrappers and I can't believe I did it again. It's really embarrassing, honestly. I feel a lot of shame about it.
Do you feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during these episodes?

Yes, definitely. I eat so fast during those times that I... I barely even taste anything. I'll just be standing there at the dining room table, surrounded by the microwave and boxes, and I'm just swallowing one bite while I'm already reaching for the next. It's very rushed.
Do you remember everything that happens while you're eating during these episodes?

Yes, I remember everything. I mean, it's not like I black out or anything. I'm fully aware that I'm doing it, even if it feels out of control in the moment. I just... I know exactly what I'm eating, I just can't seem to make myself stop.
Do you enjoy the taste of the food while you're eating during these episodes?
No, not really. Like I said before, I eat so fast I barely taste it. It's not about enjoying the food, it's just about eating it. I don't think I'm really paying attention to how it tastes at all.
Do you feel like you're eating in secret during these episodes because you're ashamed of how much you're eating?

Yes, absolutely. I make a point of doing it when my husband is asleep, or when the contractors are gone for the day. I would just be mortified for anyone to actually see the amount of food I can put away. I spend all day at work acting so controlled, so... yeah, having someone see me like that is out of the question. I definitely hide it.
Do you feel like you have no control over what you're eating or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes. Once I start, there is this awful switch that flips. I can actually be standing there thinking to myself, Taylor, put it away, but... my hands just keep opening containers anyway. It really feels like I am not the one in charge.
Do you think you might be using food as a way to cope with or escape from your emotions during these episodes?

I don't know. I guess I've never really thought about it like that. I mean, I'm stressed, sure. Managing the office and dealing with the contractors at the house... it's a lot. But I don't know if I'm eating because I'm upset or if it's just... something that happens. I haven't really noticed a connection like that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

No, not really. I mean, my weight fluctuates a few pounds here and there like anyone else's, but... no, I haven't noticed any major changes. It's stayed pretty much the same over time, even with all the eating.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen?

Well, I actually keep a journal, so I can see the pattern. When I look back through it, um... there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. And, honestly, most weeks it happens several times.
Have you ever tried to make up for these episodes of eating a lot by doing things like exercising more, vomiting, or using laxatives?

No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything... and I'm definitely not exercising extra to make up for it. I usually just go to sleep or sit there feeling bad about what I just did. So, no, none of those things.
For how long have you been experiencing these episodes of eating a large amount of food?
This has been going on since we started remodeling our kitchen, which was about ten months ago.
Can you think of any specific emotions or events that might trigger these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I've tried to look for a pattern, especially since I keep that journal, but... I haven't really noticed anything specific that sets it off. It just seems to happen whether I've had a really stressful day at the office or a totally normal, fine one. So, no, I can't really pinpoint a specific emotion or event.
Do you think these episodes happen more often during particularly stressful periods at work or with the contractors?

Not really, no. Like I was just saying, it doesn't seem to matter. I mean, I could have a terrible week with the contractors or a really heavy workload at the office, and it happens... but it also happens just as much when things are completely quiet and fine. So, I don't think the stress is making it happen more often. It's just kind of a constant thing right now.
Have you ever had one of these episodes of eating a large amount of food where you didn't feel guilty or ashamed afterwards?

No, I can't think of a single time. Every time it happens, I feel... well, just awful about it afterwards. The guilt is always there once I realize how much I've eaten. So, no, I've never had an episode where I didn't feel ashamed.
Do you think these episodes of eating a large amount of food are more likely to happen on days when you're feeling emotionally upset or on days when you're feeling calm?

Honestly, it's just like I was saying a minute ago. It really doesn't seem to lean one way or the other. I can be completely calm, having a perfectly fine day, and it happens... or I can be really upset about something, and it still happens. There just isn't a difference that I can see.
